subtopics.name: Controlled/Uncontrolled Forms
subtopics.content: Controlled components are form elements whose value is handled by React state. Uncontrolled components maintain their own internal state and are accessed using refs. Controlled components are the recommended approach for most scenarios in React.

subtopics.name: Form Validation
subtopics.content: Form validation ensures that user input meets specific criteria before being submitted. In React, this is often handled by checking state values during change events or upon form submission, and displaying error messages accordingly.

subtopics.name: CSS in React
subtopics.content: There are several ways to style React components, including traditional CSS files, CSS Modules for local scoping, and CSS-in-JS libraries. Each approach has its own benefits for organizing and maintaining styles.

subtopics.name: Tailwind / Bootstrap
subtopics.content: Tailwind CSS and Bootstrap are popular frameworks that can be integrated into React projects to speed up UI development. Tailwind uses utility-first classes, while Bootstrap provides a set of pre-designed components.

subtopics.name: Dynamic Styling
subtopics.content: Dynamic styling allows you to change the appearance of components based on state or props. This can be achieved by conditionally applying class names or using inline style objects that depend on component data.

subtopics.name: Responsive UI
subtopics.content: Building a responsive UI involves using techniques like media queries and flexible layouts (Flexbox/Grid) to ensure the application looks good on all devices, from mobile phones to desktop monitors.

subtopics.name: Reusable Components
subtopics.content: One of the core strengths of React is the ability to create reusable UI components. By passing props, you can create modular components like Buttons, Inputs, and Cards that can be used throughout the application with different configurations.
